setup.zh: 开春，舅舅从县城来，念了一张告示：沉鼎观开山门，录为弟子者，家里每年五两银子。他刚念到「沉鼎」，你胸口的木牌烫得像一块炭。
setup.en: In spring Uncle comes from the county town and reads out a notice: Chending Temple opens its gate, and a disciple's family gets five taels a year. At the words "Chending" the token at your chest burns like a coal.

recap.zh: 舅舅带来了沉鼎观开山门的告示；他念到「沉鼎」，木牌烫得像炭——你决定去。
recap.en: Uncle brought the notice that Chending Temple would open its gate; at "Chending" the token burned like a coal — and you decided to go.

zh: 舅舅：簇新的青布长衫，二斤肉，一包红糖。
en: Uncle: a brand-new blue gown, two jin of meat, a packet of brown sugar.
"…present themselves for trial at the foot of Chending Mountain."
Between your fingers, a thread of silver light.

story.zh:
开春的时候，舅舅来了。

他穿一身簇新的青布长衫，手里提着二斤肉、一包红糖，站在沈家门口，看了看那扇装歪了的门，拿袖子掩着鼻子，咳了一声。

小满他爹慌慌张张地迎出来，拿袖子擦炕沿，擦了三遍，才请他坐。舅舅坐是坐下了，屁股却只沾了半边，另外半边悬在空中，随时准备撤退。他看了看屋顶，看了看墙角接水的那一排盆——十七个，一个不少，整整齐齐地排着，像一队站岗的兵——又看了看姐夫缠着麻布的膝盖，长长地叹了一口气，说道：「姐，你这日子……」

小满他娘道：「挺好。」

「屋顶都漏成这样了——」

「通风。」

「这墙都裂了——」

「透亮。」

舅舅张了张嘴，竟没接上话来。他瞧着他姐姐，瞧了半天，压低了声音道：「姐，你当年要是听爹的话——」

他娘道：「吃饭。」

舅舅便闭上了嘴。小满在旁边听着，心里一动。外公的话，是什么话？他娘当年，没听外公什么话？他看看他娘，他娘正低头给舅舅盛饭，盛得满满的，脸上什么也看不出来。他又看看他爹，他爹正低着头，一下一下地揉膝盖，揉得很慢，揉得很用力。

吃饭的时候，舅舅从怀里摸出一张折得方方正正的纸，说道：「县城贴的告示。我给你们抄了一份。」清了清嗓子，念道：

「**沉鼎观**，三年一开山门，收徒。凡十二至十六岁、身家清白者，皆可于九月初九，赴泗水沉鼎山下应试。录为弟子者，其家每岁由观中发给白银五两——」

他刚念到「沉鼎」两个字，小满胸口的木牌登时烫得像一块刚从灶膛里扒出来的炭。那一冬它烫过三回，这一回，比那三回加起来还烫，烫得小满「嗷——！」的一声从凳子上蹦了起来，一口饭，不偏不倚，全喷在了舅舅脸上。

屋里霎时间安静了下来。

舅舅坐在那儿，脸上挂着饭粒，一动不动。一粒米从他的眉毛上慢慢地滑了下来，滑过鼻梁，滑到鼻尖上，停住了，停了一停，才掉进他面前那碗饭里。

小满捂着胸口道：「……噎、噎着了。」

舅舅很慢很慢地从怀里掏出一块帕子——那帕子上也是一股药味——擦着脸，一面擦，一面道：「这孩子。吃个饭都吃不利索。」他擦完了，瞧了瞧碗里那粒米，又瞧了瞧小满，终于还是把那碗饭端起来，吃了。济世堂的账房，是不糟蹋粮食的。

没有人看见，小满捂在胸口的手指缝里，漏出了一线银光。木牌上那条银色的尾巴，不再一明一暗了。它亮着，一直亮着，亮得发烫，像一个在梦里找了很久很久的人，终于听见了自己要找的那个名字。

小满他娘问道：「五两银子？」

舅舅道：「一年五两。」

小满他爹放下了筷子。沈家一年交马家的租，折成银子，不过二两多一点；加上山风钱，加上这个钱那个钱，也不过三两。五两银子，是沈家两年的命。

舅舅压低了声音，又道：「还有。家里有孩子进了仙门的——马家，不敢收租。」

屋里静了。

隔了一会儿，舅舅才道：「姐。二十年前，我也去过。」

一家三口全都愣住了。

他接着说道：「那年我十四。三百级石阶，要在一炷香里走完。我爬到一百六十级，腿就动不了了。我在那儿坐了一炷香，看着别人一个一个从我身边走过去。然后我就下山了，去济世堂学打算盘。」

他说这话的时候，眼睛看着桌上那碗饭，声音很平，平得像在念账本上的一行字。

小满他娘轻轻地道：「上回你说是一百五十级。」

「……一百六十级。」

「上上回，一百四十。」

舅舅的脸登时红了，红得跟他提来的那二斤肉一个颜色：「每年都在长嘛！人老了，记性好了！」

小满他爹在旁很真诚地道：「那再过几年，您就爬上去了。」

舅舅瞪了姐夫一眼。姐夫便低头吃饭。

舅舅转过头来看着小满，看了一会儿，说道：「你娘识字，你随她，脑子比我活。你爹打猎，你随他，腿脚比我稳。去试试。进不去，也不亏什么。进去了——」

他没说完。他看了一眼姐夫的膝盖，又看了一眼墙角那一排盆，又看了一眼他姐姐那件短了一截袖子的棉袄，便低下头，吃饭了。
story.en:
In spring, his uncle came.

He wore a brand-new blue cloth gown and carried two catties of meat and a packet of brown sugar, and stood at the Shens' door looking at the crooked door, sleeve over his nose, and coughed.

Xiaoman's father hurried out in a fluster, wiped the edge of the kang with his sleeve three times, and only then asked him to sit. His uncle sat — but only half his backside touched, the other half hanging in the air, ready to retreat at any moment. He looked at the roof, at the row of basins in the corner catching drips — seventeen, not one missing, lined up neat as a squad of sentries — at his brother-in-law's hemp-bound knee, and heaved a long sigh. "Sister, this life of yours…"

Xiaoman's mother said, "It's fine."

"The roof's leaking like this —"

"Ventilation."

"The walls are cracked —"

"Lets the light in."

His uncle opened his mouth and for once had no reply. He looked at his sister a long time and lowered his voice. "Sister, if you'd listened to Father back then —"

His mother said, "Eat."

His uncle shut his mouth. Xiaoman, listening to one side, was struck. Grandfather's words — what words? What hadn't his mother listened to, back then? He looked at his mother; she was dishing rice for his uncle, piling the bowl high, her face showing nothing. He looked at his father; his father had his head down, rubbing his knee over and over, very slowly, very hard.

Over the meal his uncle took from his coat a sheet of paper folded square. "A notice posted in the county town. I copied it out for you." He cleared his throat and read:

"**Chending Temple** opens its mountain gate once every three years to take disciples. All between twelve and sixteen years of age, of clean family, may present themselves for trial at the foot of Chending Mountain on the Si River on the ninth day of the ninth month. For those enrolled as disciples, the Temple will grant their family five taels of silver each year —"

The moment he read the word *Chending*, the token at Xiaoman's chest burned like a coal just raked from the stove. It had burned three times that winter; this time was hotter than all three together, so hot that Xiaoman leapt off his stool with a yelp — and a mouthful of rice went, squarely, all over his uncle's face.

The room went dead quiet at once.

His uncle sat there with rice on his face, perfectly still. One grain slid slowly down from his eyebrow, over the bridge of his nose to the tip, paused there, and dropped into the bowl in front of him.

Xiaoman clutched his chest. "…I ch-choked."

Very, very slowly his uncle took out a handkerchief — it smelled of medicine too — and wiped his face, saying as he wiped, "This child. Can't even eat a meal properly." When he'd finished he looked at the grain in his bowl, then at Xiaoman, and in the end picked up the bowl and ate it. The bookkeeper of the Jishi Hall does not waste grain.

Nobody saw the thread of silver light leaking between the fingers Xiaoman pressed to his chest. The silver tail on the token no longer went bright and dim. It was lit, and stayed lit, burning hot, like someone who has searched a long, long time in a dream and at last heard the very name they were looking for.

Xiaoman's mother asked, "Five taels of silver?"

His uncle said, "Five taels a year."

Xiaoman's father put down his chopsticks. The Shens' rent to the Mas, in silver, came to a little over two taels a year; add the mountain-wind money, and this money and that money, still no more than three. Five taels was two years of the Shens' life.

His uncle lowered his voice again. "And. A family with a child who's got into an immortal sect — the Mas daren't take rent from them."

The room went quiet.

After a while his uncle said, "Sister. Twenty years ago, I went too."

All three of them stared.

He went on: "I was fourteen. Three hundred stone steps, to be climbed within one stick of incense. I got to step one hundred and sixty, and my legs wouldn't move. I sat there the length of a stick of incense, watching others walk past me one by one. Then I came down the mountain and went to the Jishi Hall to learn the abacus."

As he said it his eyes were on the bowl of rice on the table, his voice very flat, flat as reading out a line of a ledger.

Xiaoman's mother said softly: "Last time you said a hundred and fifty."

"…A hundred and sixty."

"The time before, a hundred and forty."

His uncle's face went red at once, red as the two catties of meat he'd brought: "It grows every year! Getting older, my memory's getting better!"

Xiaoman's father said, quite sincerely, "Then in a few more years you'll have got to the top."

His uncle glared at his brother-in-law. His brother-in-law lowered his head and ate.

His uncle turned and looked at Xiaoman a while. "Your mother can read — you take after her, a quicker head than mine. Your father hunts — you take after him, steadier legs than mine. Go and try. If you don't get in, you've lost nothing. If you do —"

He didn't finish. He looked at his brother-in-law's knee, at the row of basins in the corner, at his sister's coat with its too-short sleeves, and lowered his head and ate.

exits.means: decides to go to the temple trials

story.zh:
那天夜里，小满躺在炕上，一直睁着眼睛。

他在心里算账，像他娘教他的那样，一笔一笔地算。

五两银子，一年。他爹，再也不用拖着那条腿进深山；他娘，下雨天再也不用把家里十七个盆都摆出来；马三的短棍，再也敲不到沈家的门框；那件棉袄，今年冬天便有了，袖子不短，手腕不冻。

然后，是另一笔账。

他把木牌从衣领里掏出来，贴在耳朵边上听。什么都听不见，可它亮着。那条银色的尾巴，从晌午舅舅念告示的时候亮起来，一直亮到这时候，一刻也没暗过。一冬天了，它从来没有亮得这么久过。

它在等他。

「……本王在找一个地方……一个名字……等你听见了，本王会知道的。」

他听见了。她也知道了。

他对着黑暗，小声说道：「好。我去。」

木牌暖了一下。

他爹把锄头往地上一拄，道：「你是追兔子的走法。追兔子，要快，兔子跑三步，你得跑五步。可兔子跑不远，跑一阵子，它自己就趴下了，你也趴下了。」他指了指山上，「追鹿不是这样。鹿走得稳，走得远，一走一天。你跟它比快，跑到晌午，你趴下了，它还在走。你得跟它比稳。」

他教小满走：三步一吸，三步一呼。吸的时候，气往下沉；呼的时候，脚往前送。不看坡顶，只看脚底下这一级。一级一级地走，一口一口地喘，喘得跟脚步一个节拍。

小满照着走了一回，走到坡顶，竟真的不大喘了。他回头看那几十级歪歪扭扭的石阶，觉得它们比方才矮了许多。

他爹道：「山上的路，都是这么走完的。」

小满不信。他爹便把蒲扇搁下，道：「你再听。狼嚎，是从胸口里出来的。它先吸一口气，吸得满满的，再从胸口里一点一点往外推，推出来的声音，是热的，是有气的，你隔着一座山都听得出，那是一个活物在喊。风不是。风钻石缝，钻出来的声音再响，也是空的。它没有胸口，它只有一个洞。」

小满闭上眼睛，又听了一回。那嚎叫声忽高忽低，一声接一声，可他听着听着，便听出来了：那声音里没有换气。一个活物喊了这么久，总要换一口气；这声音却一口气也不换，只是一个劲儿地响，响得又尖又长，又空又冷。

他睁开眼睛道：「是空的。」

他爹点了点头，又摇起了蒲扇，道：「山里的东西，十样里有九样是吓唬人的。你闭上眼，听哪一样是从胸口里出来的。那一样，才是真的。」

小满那天夜里记住了这句话。他不知道自己记住的是什么。他要到许多许多年以后，站在一个比那天夜里的后山大得多的地方，面对一样比狼可怕得多的东西，才会想起这句话来，才会明白，他爹那天夜里教他的，是这一辈子最要紧的一样本事。
story.en:
That night Xiaoman lay on the kang with his eyes open.

He did the accounts in his head, as his mother had taught him, item by item.

Five taels of silver, a year. His father would never again have to drag that leg into the deep mountains; his mother would never again, on rainy days, set out all seventeen basins; Ma San's club would never again rap the Shens' doorframe; the coat would be there this winter, sleeves long enough, wrists not frozen.

And then, the other account.

He took the token out from his collar and held it to his ear. He heard nothing, but it was lit. The silver tail had lit up at noon when his uncle read the notice, and stayed lit till now, not dimming for a moment. All winter it had never been lit so long.

It was waiting for him.

"…This king is looking for a place… a name… when you hear it, this king will know."

He had heard it. And she knew.

Into the dark he said softly: "All right. I'll go."

The token warmed, once.

His father planted the hoe on the ground. "You walk like you're chasing a hare. Chasing a hare you must be quick — the hare runs three steps, you run five. But a hare can't run far; after a bit it lies down of itself, and so do you." He pointed up the mountain. "Chasing a deer isn't like that. A deer walks steady, walks far, walks all day. Race it for speed and by noon you're lying down and it's still walking. You have to race it for steadiness."

He taught Xiaoman to walk: three steps a breath in, three steps a breath out. Breathing in, the qi sinks down; breathing out, the feet go forward. Don't look at the top of the slope; look only at the step under your feet. Step by step, breath by breath, the breathing in time with the feet.

Xiaoman walked it once that way, and reaching the top wasn't really out of breath at all. He looked back at the dozens of crooked stone steps and they seemed a good deal lower than before.

His father said, "Every road on the mountain gets walked like this."

Xiaoman didn't believe him. So his father put down the fan. "Listen again. A wolf's howl comes out of its chest. It draws a breath first, fills up full, then pushes it out of its chest bit by bit; the sound that comes out is warm, has breath in it; even across a mountain you can hear it's a living thing calling. Wind's not like that. Wind drilling through a crack in the rock — however loud it comes out, it's hollow. It hasn't got a chest; it's only got a hole."

Xiaoman shut his eyes and listened again. The howling rose and fell, one after another, and as he listened he heard it: there was no breath taken in it. Anything alive, calling that long, has to take a breath; this sound took none, only kept on, shrill and long, hollow and cold.

He opened his eyes. "It's hollow."

His father nodded and took up the fan again. "Of ten things in the mountains, nine are there to scare you. Shut your eyes and listen for which one comes out of a chest. That one's the real one."

Xiaoman remembered that saying that night. He didn't know what it was he'd remembered. Not until many, many years later, standing somewhere much bigger than the back hill that night, facing something far more terrible than a wolf, would he remember it, and understand that what his father taught him that night was the most important skill of his life.

exits.means: hesitates, decides not to go yet, waits

story.zh:
那天夜里，小满躺在炕上，对着黑暗，小声道：「不去……家里离不开我。再等三年。」

胸口的木牌，一下子凉了。那条亮了一整晚的尾巴，暗了下去——一明，一暗，一明——暗下去的那一下，比平时长。

他睁着眼睛躺到天亮。隔着一道布帘，他爹咳了半夜。
story.en:
That night Xiaoman lay on the kang and said softly into the dark: "I won't go… home can't do without me. Wait another three years."

The token at his chest went cold at once. The tail that had been lit all evening dimmed — bright, dim, bright — and the dim lasted longer than usual.

He lay with his eyes open till dawn. Through the cloth curtain his father coughed half the night.
